about: In the prayers at the foot of the altar, Psalm 42 in the Vulgate numbering (Psalm 43 in Hebrew) is said alternately by the priest and server. The antiphon “Introíbo ad altáre Dei” precedes it and is repeated after the doxology. In Masses for the Dead, and at Masses of the season from Passion Sunday through Maundy Thursday, the psalm is left out with its antiphon and the Confíteor follows at once.

s01.narrative: At Masses for the Dead, and at Masses of the season from Passion Sunday through Maundy Thursday, the psalm, the Glória Patri and the repetition of the antiphon are omitted. After In nómine Patris, the antiphon and the Adiutórium, the Confíteor follows at once.

s02.narrative: The priest says the psalm alternately with the ministers.

s03.translation: Judge me, O God, and decide my case against an unholy people. Deliver me from an unjust and deceitful man.

s04.translation: For You, O God, are my strength. Why have You rejected me, and why do I walk in sorrow while the enemy oppresses me?

s05.translation: Send forth Your light and Your truth. They have led me and brought me to Your holy mountain and into Your dwelling places.

s06.translation: And I will go to the altar of God, to God, who gladdens my youth.

s07.translation: I will praise You on the lyre, O God, my God. Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you disturb me?

s08.translation: Hope in God, for I will yet praise Him. He is the salvation of my countenance and my God.

s09.translation: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

s10.translation: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

s12.translation: I will go to the altar of God.

s13.translation: To God, who gladdens my youth.

w011.function: Ablative. With “gente” (w009), it forms the phrase “an unholy nation”.

w020.function: The expressed pronoun emphasizes the subject: “Thou”.

w030.function: Masculine nominative. The Latin form can also be feminine, but the corresponding Hebrew and Greek forms are masculine.

w035.function: Nominative, serving as the subject of “afflígit” (w033).

w042.function: The neuter plural differs from the gender of “lucem” (w037) and “veritátem” (w040). It corresponds to Greek αὐτά in the Septuagint.

w044.function: Third-person plural perfect. Its subjects are “lucem” (w037) and “veritátem” (w040).

w047.function: “In” with the accusative marks direction of motion.

w056.function: In the Mass this verse serves as the antiphon before and after the psalm.

w059.function: A genitive dependent on “altáre” (w058): the altar of God.

w062.function: Nominative and the subject of “lætíficat” (w063). Its antecedent “Deum” (w061) is accusative.

w064.function: The Hebrew text speaks of joy, while “youth” appears in the Septuagint, which the Latin follows here.

w066.function: The verb “confitéri” can mean “confess” or “praise”. Here it bears the latter sense.

w072.function: The form “meus” is nominative. Its regular masculine vocative is “mi”, which the psalter does not use here.

w076.function: Vocative: the psalmist addresses his own soul.

w082.function: An imperative addressed to ánima mea in the preceding sentence.

w089.function: Nominative in an apposition referring to “illi” (w088).

w090.function: A 4th-declension genitive, with the same form as the nominative. “mei” (w091) confirms the case.

w093.function: Nominative. Together with “salutáre” (w089), it refers to “illi” (w088).

w095.function: Nominative in a verbless sentence. The sense is: may glory be.

w096.function: Dative marking the recipient of glory.

w111.function: A preposition with the accusative, forming part of the phrase “unto ages of ages”.
